title: Landing copy — Inference economics experiment kit
body:
Goal: rapid iterate high-converting homepage and product page copy that foregrounds Redwood’s core sales thesis — inference is a controllable cost/latency problem, not just model selection. This doc collects distinct headline variants, support lines, product page modules, and competitive talking points to A/B test over the next six weeks.

Audience & tone:
- Primary: engineering and ML platform leads evaluating inference providers. Secondary: product engineering managers and platform procurement leads.
- Tone: technical but pragmatic — avoid hype. Use quantifiable claims, clear trade-offs, and operational language (SLOs, latency, throughput, cost per token, SLA).

Testing framework (KPI-oriented):
- Primary metric: signups from engineering trial flows (dev API key requests).
- Secondary metrics: demo requests, time on product-page, bounce on pricing block.
- Test cadence: ship 2 headline variants + 2 supporting value-prop blocks weekly. Measure 7-day convert lift.

Hero headline candidates (short, 5–9 words):
1) "Make LLM inference predictable and affordable"
2) "Ship fast, pay less for real-time LLMs"
3) "High-throughput inference without surprise bills"
4) "Engineered for production-scale LLM economics"
5) "Latency-first inference for product teams"

One-line supports (to pair with headlines):
A) "Unified runtime for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — transparent latencies and per-route cost controls."
B) "Autoscaling GPU pools, KV caching, and batching that cut per-token costs while keeping latency SLOs."
C) "Model rollouts, traceable regressions, and cost-aware routing built for engineering teams."
D) "Benchmarked throughput and latency profiles so you can pick the right model variant for the job."

CTA permutations:
- Try the hosted API (free credits)
- Start a dedicated capacity trial
- Book a 20-minute infra walkthrough
- See latency & cost benchmarks

Hero microcopy experiments (short trust signals under CTA):
- "Free credits — no card required"
- "Used in production by multi-region SaaS teams"
- "Benchmarks validated on common LLM workloads"

Top-of-page value-prop blocks (modular, test separately):
- Performance: "Predictable latency SLOs — 50ms tail for short turns on Dedicated (typical)."
- Cost controls: "Per-route batching, KV caching, and intelligent routing that reduce token spend by 30–60% depending on workload."
- Deployment modes: "Hosted API, Reserved Dedicated pools, and Private VPC/on-prem deploys with KMS integrations."
- Operations: "Per-token tracing, rollout A/B, auto-fallbacks, and regression alerts tied to eval sets."

Product page modules (order for scannability):
1) Quick summary + 1-line benefits
2) How it works (3 bullets): runtime optimizations, smart routing, caching & batching
3) Real metrics (benchmarks): latency distributions, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M tokens for typical prompts
4) Use cases and archetypes (SaaS chat, embeddings at scale, customer-facing summarization)
5) Pricing summary + CTA
6) Trust & compliance (SLA, SOC2, KMS, on-prem option)

Competitive framing — short notes for copy and sales enablement (one-sentence each):
- General cloud AI platforms: "Broad model access, but limited inference-optimized runtime — you may pay for latency or build ops yourself."
- LLM API providers focused on simplicity: "Great for prototypes; less control for production economics and private deployments."
- Self-hosted inference vendors: "Deep runtime optimization but high ops burden; Redwood offers the same production primitives with managed options and private deployments."

Differentiation hooks to surface on page (prioritized):
1) "Unified interface across hosted, dedicated, and private — same SDK, same rollout controls."
2) "Cost levers you can control — batching, caching, quantization recommendations tied to your workload."
3) "Operational guarantees — rollback, canary, and fallback policies built-in."

Copy micro-angles to test (rotate weekly):
- Economic-first: emphasize cost-per-token savings and predictable billing.
- Reliability-first: emphasize fallbacks, SLA, and multi-region continuity.
- Control-first: emphasize private deployments, KMS, and network isolation.

Landing layout experiments (two variants):
Variant A — 'Economics lead'
- Hero with big cost claim + CTA
- Single row: three cards (latency, cost, deployments) with KPIs
- Benchmarks carousel
- Customer logos + short quote
- Quickstart + pricing CTA

Variant B — 'Reliability lead'
- Hero with reliability claim + CTA
- Timeline of failover/fallback behavior (visual)
- Feature deep-dive (rollouts, tracing, alerts)
- Case study highlight (short)

Copy dos and don’ts:
- DO use numbers where possible (latency, percent savings).
- DO use operational vocabulary for trust (SLO, SLA, traces).
- DON’T claim platform lock-in or make unverifiable performance guarantees.
- DON’T use vague superlatives without context ("fastest").

Short competitive rebuttal snippets for FAQs (copy-ready):
- Q: "Why not run inference myself?"
  A: "If you need fast iteration + predictable unit economics, building a production-grade inference stack is high-opportunity cost. Redwood gives you the runtime and controls without months of ops work."
- Q: "How do you compare on cost?"
  A: "Cost depends on workload. We show per-route benchmarks and recommended batching/cache configs so you can estimate spend before committing."

Suggested A/B test matrix (first 6 weeks):
- Week 1–2: Hero headline A vs B, support line A vs B
- Week 3–4: Value-prop block order + CTA microcopy
- Week 5–6: Layout A vs B + trust microcopy under CTA

Notes for creative team:
- Assets needed: benchmark charts (CSV), short customer quotes (1–2 lines), logos (SVG), short demo GIF showing latency dashboard.
- Keep hero illustrations minimal; prefer schematic diagrams (routing, caching) over generic stock images.

Open questions / research to complete before first iteration:
- Collect three representative prompt workloads (chat short-turn, long completion, embeddings batch) and run cost+latency sims to produce concrete numbers for hero/support lines.
- Confirm any SLA language and exact uptime SLA.
- Gather quotes and logos from three early customers that permit use on homepage.

Appendix: quick list of headline-to-CTA pairings to ship as test cells:
- "Make LLM inference predictable and affordable" + "Try the hosted API (free credits)"
- "Ship fast, pay less for real-time LLMs" + "See latency & cost benchmarks"
- "Engineered for production-scale LLM economics" + "Book a 20-minute infra walkthrough"

End — draft for first-run experiments. Use this as canonical source for copy tests and iterate based on early funnel metrics.
